summary: The Index of qualitative variation calculator works out the index of qualitative variation (IQV). It uses the sum of all squared percentages, the sum of all squared percentages (∑p²), the category 1 and the category 2. It is built for an assignment, a report or a data discussion where you need a defensible number. The results leave the screen the moment you edit a field; press Calculate and they come back updated, so a single changed input shows its own effect.

sections.title: How does the Index of qualitative variation calculator work?
sections.html:
The Index of qualitative variation calculator takes the values in the form, applies the relationship described below and reports the index of qualitative variation (IQV) in the results panel.

Working from the top of the form: you choose the option that describes your case (the input type and number of categories); then you type in the sum of all squared percentages (∑p²), the sum of all squared percentages (∑p²) (2), the category 1 and the category 2.

The arithmetic runs locally each time an input changes. The page knows which values you have given it and which it still has to derive, so the results panel is never stale.

sections.title: The formula behind the Index of qualitative variation calculator
sections.html:
One relationship drives the whole page:

The index of qualitative variation (IQV)=((1 ÷ 10000) × number of categories × (10000 − the sum of all squared percentages (∑p²)) ÷ (number of categories − 1))

Read it as an ordinary equation. Where a word appears instead of a letter, it is the label of one of the boxes in the form; where a function appears, it is the usual mathematical meaning of that function.

sections.title: What is a worked example?
sections.html:
Take Input type set to Sum of percentages, Number of categories set to 2, The sum of all squared percentages (∑p²) = 10 and Category 1 = 10. The calculator returns The index of qualitative variation (IQV) = 1.998.

Read it as a template. Every number above can be replaced with one of yours; only the relationship between them is fixed.

  1. Enter the values listed above, matching the units each box asks for.
  2. Read off the result. Any field you leave empty is the one the calculator solves for.
  3. Sanity-check the number against the relationship: The index of qualitative variation (IQV) = 1.998 should be roughly the size you expected from Input type set to Sum of percentages and Number of categories set to 2.

If a number looks wrong, check three things in this order: that the units match what you had in mind, that no drop-down is still on its default, and that the value you entered is on the same scale as the rest — a rate typed as 5 rather than 0.05 is the classic mistake. Those three account for almost every answer that is out by a factor.

sections.title: When should you use it?
sections.html:
The Index of qualitative variation calculator earns its place in the middle of a task, not instead of one. It is most useful when:

  • Deciding how much confidence a sample really supports
  • Checking a result a piece of software produced
  • Turning raw numbers into something you can quote
  • Any time the same 4 figures keep coming back — the sum of all squared percentages, the sum of all squared percentages (∑p²) and the category 1 — and you would rather not repeat the arithmetic by hand each time.

sections.title: How do you get a reliable answer?
sections.html:
• Round only at the end. The calculator carries full precision internally, so re-entering a value you already rounded is the fastest way to introduce drift.
  • Compare two scenarios by changing the input that actually differs between them, and keep the rest fixed, so the difference you see is the difference you meant to test.
  • Write the answer down with its unit. A bare number copied into a report later is exactly where units get lost.
  • Change one input at a time when you are exploring. Two simultaneous changes make it impossible to tell which one moved the result.

sections.title: What else is worth knowing?
sections.html:
• Answers that depend on a drop-down reflect the option you picked, not a range. Switching to a neighbouring option is the quickest way to see how much that factor matters.
  • Some options are backed by reference tables that ship with the page, so the values are fixed data rather than a live lookup.

faq.q: What does the Index of qualitative variation calculator work out?
faq.a: It returns the index of qualitative variation (IQV), derived from the sum of all squared percentages, the sum of all squared percentages (∑p²) and the category 1. Every field in the form feeds the same relationship: press Calculate once and changing any of them updates the result immediately, with no page reload.

faq.q: What do I need to enter to use the Index of qualitative variation calculator?
faq.a: The form asks for the sum of all squared percentages, the sum of all squared percentages (∑p²), the category 1 and the category 2, which is 20 fields in total. Each one is labelled with what it means and, where relevant, the unit it expects. Anything you leave blank is treated as the value to solve for.

faq.q: How much do the drop-down choices change the answer?
faq.a: There are several choices to make (2 in total), and each one selects a different case rather than scaling the result. Switching a single option and watching the result is the fastest way to see how much that choice is worth.

With the values the page starts from, the calculator reports The index of qualitative variation (IQV) = 1.998. Treat that as a reference point rather than a recommendation: it exists so you can tell at a glance whether your own inputs are on the same scale.

faq.q: Is the Index of qualitative variation calculator free to use?
faq.a: Yes — no account, no sign-up and no limit on how many times you run it. The arithmetic happens in your browser, so the values you type are not sent anywhere.

faq.q: Do I have to fill in every box?
faq.a: Fill in the ones you know. The result boxes are computed from them, so you never enter a value the formula can derive — press Calculate and every result updates together.
